# PSE&G Responding as Thanksgiving Storm Moves Through New Jersey


## *Crews working around the clock to safely restore power and support customers through the holiday*


(NEWARK, N.J. – Nov. 26, 2026) – PSE&G crews are actively responding to outages as a strong coastal storm brings high winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding to parts of New Jersey on Thanksgiving Day. PSE&G mobilized **** nearly 3,000 **** personnel ahead of the storm to support response and restoration efforts, including line workers, tree crews and other field and support personnel. Operations teams continue to monitor weather conditions and system performance, adjusting resources and deploying crews where they are needed.


As of 7:00 p.m on Thursday, Nov. 26, approximately **17,562** PSE&G customers are without power, and **40,073** customers have been restored since the storm began.


PSE&G recognizes that outages can be especially disruptive during a holiday and is focused on restoring power safely and as quickly as possible. We’re grateful to the crews and employees working through Thanksgiving to support customers and communities, and we thank our customers for their patience as restoration efforts continue.


These response efforts build on PSE&G’s ongoing work to strengthen the electric system, improve reliability and resilience, and keep customer affordability in focus.


**Restoring Customers Safely and Quickly**


Weather conditions, including high winds and flooding, may make restoration and travel difficult. For the safety of employees and the public, there are restrictions on the use of aerial equipment such as bucket trucks during high winds.


PSE&G will continue to respond to outages and other emergencies as the storm moves through the region. Restoration work begins when conditions are safe for crews to perform their work.


Storm conditions can also lengthen the backyard restoration process as it becomes challenging to move people, equipment and resources into place for the necessary repairs.[Read more about why some outage restorations take longer than others.](https://energizepseg.com/2025/06/27/how-pseg-restored-power-after-record-breaking-heat-wave/)


During widespread outages, crews first assess damage across the electric system to determine restoration priorities before beginning repairs. Restoration efforts focus first on repairs that return power to the greatest number of customers, while also restoring service to critical facilities such as hospitals, emergency response agencies and other essential infrastructure.[Read more about our restoration process.](https://nj.pseg.com/outageandgasleaks/duringanoutage/powerrestorationprocess)


Customers should never touch or approach a downed power line. Always assume it is energized and dangerous, stay at least 30 feet away and report it immediately. Portable generators should be used only outdoors and well away from windows, doors and vents to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.


**Keeping Customers Informed**


Throughout the storm, PSE&G will remain in close communication with county and local emergency management officials and other public safety partners to help coordinate response efforts as needed.


PSE&G’s customer-facing teams, including representatives in the call center and across the company’s communications channels, will provide updates as conditions and restoration efforts progress.


Customers can report outages and monitor restoration progress by:


- Using the PSE&G mobile app
- Visiting pseg.com/outagecenter
- Texting “OUT” to 4PSEG (47734)
- Calling 1-800-436-PSEG (7734)


Customers are encouraged to sign up for outage alerts to receive updates by text, email or phone and follow PSE&G on social media:[@PSEG](https://www.facebook.com/PSEG/) on Facebook and[Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/pseg/?hl=en) and[@PSEGdelivers](https://x.com/PSEGdelivers?lang=en) on X.


PSE&G will continue to provide updates through its Outage Center, mobile app and social media channels as conditions warrant.


Customers can find their estimated time of restoration on the[PSE&G Outage map](https://outagecenter.pseg.com/external/default.html) or by texting “STAT” to 4PSEG or 47734.


For additional storm safety information, outage updates and restoration information, visit[pseg.com/outagecenter](https://nj.pseg.com/outageandgasleaks) .


Emergency preparedness is important for families, too. The PSEG Foundation and Sesame Workshop offer research-based extreme-weather preparedness resources to help young children and families build resilience and navigate weather-related emergencies. The resources include educational videos, family guides and printable activities designed to make preparedness accessible and age appropriate.


For more information and to access these resources, visit[Sesame Workshop's PSEG Foundation partnership page](https://sesameworkshop.org/about-us/partners/pseg-foundation/) .


**About PSE&G**


Public Service Electric & Gas Co. is New Jersey’s oldest and largest gas and electric delivery public utility, as well as one of the nation’s largest utilities. PSE&G has won the ReliabilityOne® Award for superior electric system reliability in the Mid-Atlantic region for 25 consecutive years. In 2025, for the fourth consecutive year, J.D. Power named PSE&G number one in customer satisfaction for residential electric service in the East among large utilities.


PSE&G is a subsidiary of Public Service Enterprise Group Inc. (PSEG) (NYSE: PEG), a predominantly regulated infrastructure company named to the Dow Jones Best in Class Index for North America for 18 consecutive years ([www.pseg.com](https://landing.pseg.com/) ).
